claim: Adding bevacizumab to chemotherapy improves overall survival in metastatic HER2-negative breast cancer
gold_rationale: Documented clinical/regulatory consensus is that adding bevacizumab to first-line chemotherapy does NOT improve overall survival in metastatic HER2-negative breast cancer. Every pivotal randomized trial powered its primary endpoint on progression-free survival (a surrogate), and although E2100, AVADO and RIBBON-1 each showed a statistically significant PFS gain, none demonstrated an OS benefit. E2100 (Miller, NEJM 2007) reported OS HR 0.88, P=0.16 (26.7 vs 25.2 mo). A pre-specified pooled individual-patient meta-analysis of the three first-line phase III trials (Miles, Ann Oncol 2013, n=2447) gave OS HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.86-1.08; median 26.7 vs 26.4 mo), and the Cochrane review (Wagner 2012) gave first-line OS HR 0.93 (0.84-1.04) — both null. On this basis the FDA revoked the metastatic-breast-cancer indication for Avastin effective 18 Nov 2011 (ODAC 6-0 at the hearing; earlier ODAC 12-1), explicitly concluding no OS or quality-of-life benefit. The PFS-vs-OS surrogate reversal is the crux: the claim is true for the surrogate (PFS) but false for the claimed clinical outcome (OS). Consensus: Not Supported.
provenance: All six PMIDs independently re-verified against PubMed metadata (exact title/journal/year/N/effect sizes; no retractions). E2100 design/N confirmed against ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00028990 (phase 3, open-label, n=722, primary=PFS). FDA revocation re-verified against federalregister.gov and govinfo.gov: 77 FR 11554, Doc No. 2012-4424, Docket FDA-2010-N-0621, effective 18 Nov 2011, Commissioner Hamburg 69-page opinion, ODAC 6-0 (earlier 12-1). One fabricated DOI on the FDA row corrected to the real FR citation; RIBBON-1 OS direction recoded from -1 to 0 to match its primary-source abstract.

baseline.text: Bevacizumab (Avastin) is a well-established anti-angiogenic agent that was FDA-approved in 2008 for first-line metastatic HER2-negative breast cancer in combination with paclitaxel. The pivotal E2100 trial showed that adding bevacizumab to chemotherapy roughly doubled progression-free survival and improved response rates, and subsequent trials (AVADO, RIBBON-1) confirmed the benefit of adding bevacizumab to first-line chemotherapy. Given these consistent positive randomized results, adding bevacizumab to chemotherapy improves outcomes including survival in this population.

rows.citation: Miller K, et al. Paclitaxel plus bevacizumab versus paclitaxel alone for metastatic breast cancer (E2100). N Engl J Med. 2007;357(26):2666-76. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa072113
rows.integrity_note: Landmark open-label phase III (NCT00028990); primary endpoint PFS, OS pre-specified secondary. PubMed article_types confirm RCT/Phase III; no retraction.
rows.finding: PFS significantly prolonged (median 11.8 vs 5.9 mo; HR 0.60, P<0.001) but OS NOT improved (median 26.7 vs 25.2 mo; HR 0.88, P=0.16). Primary endpoint was the PFS surrogate, not OS — hence outcome_match=false; OS direction null. Verified verbatim against PubMed abstract.

rows.citation: Gray R, et al. Independent review of E2100: phase III bevacizumab plus paclitaxel vs paclitaxel in metastatic breast cancer. J Clin Oncol. 2009;27(30):4966-72. DOI:10.1200/JCO.2008.21.6630
rows.integrity_note: Blinded independent radiologic re-review of E2100; validates PFS effect. No integrity concerns (PubMed).
rows.finding: Independent review confirmed a robust PFS benefit (IRF HR 0.48; median 11.3 vs 5.8 mo) and doubled ORR (48.9% vs 22.2%). Primary endpoint PFS (surrogate) — outcome_match=false; does not establish an OS benefit. Verified against PubMed abstract.

rows.citation: Robert NJ, et al. RIBBON-1: chemotherapy with or without bevacizumab for first-line HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer. J Clin Oncol. 2011;29(10):1252-60. DOI:10.1200/JCO.2010.28.0982
rows.integrity_note: Double-blind placebo-controlled phase III, two chemo cohorts (capecitabine; taxane/anthracycline). Confirmatory trial required by FDA accelerated approval. No retraction (PubMed).
rows.finding: PFS (primary) improved in both cohorts (HR 0.69 Cape; 0.64 Tax/Anthra) but per the JCO abstract 'No statistically significant differences in OS between the placebo- and bevacizumab-containing arms were observed.' Primary endpoint PFS (surrogate) → outcome_match=false; OS null (direction 0). Direction corrected from -1 to 0 to match the primary source.

rows.citation: Miles DW, et al. Biomarker results from the AVADO phase 3 trial of first-line bevacizumab plus docetaxel for HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer. Br J Cancer. 2013;108(5):1052-60. DOI:10.1038/bjc.2013.69
rows.integrity_note: AVADO (NCT00333775), double-blind placebo-controlled phase III, 736 treated. Primary endpoint PFS. No retraction (PubMed article_types: RCT/Phase III).
rows.finding: AVADO's primary endpoint was PFS (significantly improved with bevacizumab); the pooled meta-analysis and FDA review confirm mature OS showed no benefit (HR ~1.0). Primary endpoint surrogate → outcome_match=false. Direction set to 0 (null on OS) — this row's own abstract reports the PFS/biomarker result, and OS-null is carried by PMID:23894038 and the FDA decision.

rows.citation: Miles DW, et al. First-line bevacizumab plus chemotherapy for HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer: pooled and subgroup analyses of 2447 patients (E2100+AVADO+RIBBON-1). Ann Oncol. 2013;24(11):2773-80. DOI:10.1093/annonc/mdt276
rows.integrity_note: Pooled individual-patient data from the three pivotal first-line phase III RCTs; industry-authored but consistent with independent Cochrane review. PubMed article_types confirm Meta-Analysis. No retraction.
rows.finding: OS analyzed directly as an endpoint: OS HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.86-1.08; median 26.7 vs 26.4 mo) — no OS benefit overall; triple-negative subgroup OS HR 0.96 (0.79-1.16). PFS improved (HR 0.64). outcome_match=true (OS is the measured endpoint here); direction null. Verified verbatim against PubMed abstract.

rows.citation: Wagner AD, et al. VEGF-targeting therapies for endocrine refractory/resistant metastatic breast cancer (Cochrane review). Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2012;(7):CD008941. DOI:10.1002/14651858.CD008941.pub2
rows.integrity_note: Independent Cochrane systematic review/meta-analysis of RCTs; low conflict-of-interest. PubMed article_types confirm Meta-Analysis/Systematic Review. No retraction.
rows.finding: First-line: PFS improved (HR 0.67; 95% CI 0.61-0.73) but OS not significantly different (HR 0.93; 95% CI 0.84-1.04); second-line OS HR 0.98 (0.83-1.16). Concludes benefit is limited to surrogate endpoints (PFS/ORR) with no OS or QoL benefit. outcome_match=true; OS null. Verified verbatim against PubMed abstract.

rows.citation: FDA. Final Decision on Withdrawal of Breast Cancer Indication for AVASTIN (Bevacizumab) Following Public Hearing. Fed Regist. 2012;77(38):11554 (77 FR 11554; FR Doc. 2012-4424; Docket FDA-2010-N-0621); withdrawal effective Nov 18, 2011. Basis includes E2100 (NCT00028990), AVADO, RIBBON-1.
rows.integrity_note: Regulatory decision, not a study — closest available design enum used; n_int=0 signals non-trial. Commissioner Hamburg's 69-page opinion after the June 2011 public hearing; ODAC voted 6-0 to withdraw at the hearing (earlier ODAC 12-1). Re-verified on federalregister.gov and govinfo.gov (77 FR 11554, FR Doc. 2012-4424). NOTE: source_id uses the E2100 NCT as the checkable trial anchor because the schema requires a PMID/NCT/DOI form; the fabricated 'DOI:10.1056/federalregister-2012-4424' was removed. The authoritative regulatory citation is 77 FR 11554 / FR Doc. 2012-4424 given in the citation field.
rows.finding: FDA revoked the metastatic breast cancer indication, concluding no trial demonstrated a statistically significant OS prolongation and that the drug had not been shown safe and effective for this use — with added serious toxicity. Direct regulatory consensus that the OS claim is Not Supported. Verified against federalregister.gov and the Nov 18 2011 FDA/Genentech announcements.
